Every statement below is a scenario that ran against the real tool; [scenarios.md](scenarios.md) has the transcripts.

> The hosted Remote MCP server for players (`mcp.spellkave.com`): an OAuth protected resource in front of the canonical PLAYER tool registry, with the public modding docs, public transcripts and world map tiles beside it.

## How it answers

- **A configuration the deployment contract forbids stops the gateway before it listens.**
  - [The gateway refuses to start when a deployment asks for another port](scenarios.md#the-gateway-refuses-to-start-when-a-deployment-asks-for-another-port)
  - [The gateway refuses to start when the world catalog is not named](scenarios.md#the-gateway-refuses-to-start-when-the-world-catalog-is-not-named)
- **An MCP answer is one JSON-RPC message in a server-sent event.**
  - [tools/list answers in one "message" event](scenarios.md#toolslist-answers-in-one-message-event)

## Commands

| Command | What it does | Scenarios (count) |
|---|---|---|
| `spellkave-player-mcp` | Start the gateway; the configuration is the environment (`SPELLKAVE_MCP_*`, `WORKOS_ISSUER`, `SPELLKAVE_WORLD_CATALOG`). Logs `spellkave-player-mcp: ready (trust-boundary=…)` and then one JSON operations line per request on stderr; SIGTERM stops it cleanly (through the tsx launcher the exit code is 143, bead sk-jay0.6.116). | 0 |
| `spellkave-player-mcp-health` | The container health check: exit 0 when `GET /healthz` answers 200, else 1. | 0 |
| `POST /mcp` | Stateless Streamable HTTP MCP (JSON-RPC in, one server-sent event out). Needs `Authorization: Bearer <AuthKit access token>`. | [22](scenarios.md#toolslist-answers-in-one-message-event) |
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[/mcp]` | RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata: the issuer to log in at and the scopes. | [2](scenarios.md#well-knownoauth-protected-resourcemcp-names-the-issuer-as-the-only-authorization-server) |
| `GET /healthz` | Readiness, redacted: `ok` or `unavailable`. | [3](scenarios.md#the-gateway-is-unavailable-while-the-issuer-is-down) |
| `GET /transcripts/<slug>` | A public world's transcript (JSONL), for logged-in spectators. | [4](scenarios.md#a-transcript-request-without-a-token-answers-401) |
| `GET /w/<slug>/…` | Map tiles, TileJSON, style and the OSM API 0.6 of a catalog world, for logged-in map clients from any origin. | [2](scenarios.md#get-wnopetilesjson-for-a-world-not-in-the-catalog-answers-404) |

**Call the gateway from a browser**

- [An allowed origin's preflight is answered without a token](scenarios.md#an-allowed-origins-preflight-is-answered-without-a-token): `OPTIONS /mcp` · [`withMcpCors`](../src/mcp-cors.ts)
  A browser sends the preflight without credentials, so it must not need one. The default allowlist is the canonical host, claude.ai, spellkave.com, www.spellkave.com and localhost.

## Rules

- **A token the gateway cannot trust is refused with 401 invalid_token.**
  - [A token for another audience is refused](scenarios.md#a-token-for-another-audience-is-refused): `{"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"aud mismatch (want one of $MCP/mcp)"}`
  - [A token from another issuer is refused](scenarios.md#a-token-from-another-issuer-is-refused): `{"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"token issuer https://authkit.staging.example.test is not the configured issuer $ISSUER"}`
  - [A token signed with a key it never saw is refused](scenarios.md#a-token-signed-with-a-key-it-never-saw-is-refused): `{"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"no JWKS key matches token kid stranger-key published by issuer $ISSUER"}`
  - [A token that expired is refused](scenarios.md#a-token-that-expired-is-refused): `{"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"Token has expired"}`
  - [A token issued before the player signed out everywhere is refused](scenarios.md#a-token-issued-before-the-player-signed-out-everywhere-is-refused): `{"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"token was issued before sign-out"}`
    Signing out on the login site writes `logout_after` into the player's WorkOS user metadata (ADR-0161 D-7). The gateway reads it, cached for 30 s per player, and refuses an older token although it has not expired; a token issued after the sign-out is let in.
- **A call the gateway can refuse by itself never reaches a world.**
